transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Nina (Redwood SE), Lucas (Redwood CSM), Maya (OptiHealth Head ML), Ethan (OptiHealth Platform Eng), Priya (OptiHealth Security), Aaron (Data Scientist)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Reviewed pilot results from last week's shadow run; discussed model pinning tradeoffs and an emergency fallback plan if latency spikes or quality regressions occur.
- Agreed to run focused latency/cost matrix for pinned model vs quantized variant; customer to share canonical prompts.
- Security questions on KMS, audit logs, and VPC routing flagged; Redwood to provide doc.

Topics:
- Current metrics and regression signals
- Model selection: base vs quantized variants vs smaller family models
- Version pinning strategies and soft rollbacks
- Emergency fallback procedures and SLA implications
- Security and deployment constraints (VPC, KMS, SOC2)

[00:00] Samir: all right hello everyone thanks for joining on a thursday. quick roll call, i'll do a very brief agenda — first go over the last week's metrics, then nina will run the latency / cost tradeoff, and we'll finish with the pinning and rollback runbook. sound good?
[00:17] Maya: yep sounds good. we had a couple of odd user reports yesterday that i want to flag early, may be related to a prompt drift.
[00:29] Nina: cool, i'll dig in on that after the metrics. i ran a shadow run overnight with the q4_2 quantized variant and saw about 18% token cost reduction but CPU tails on tail-latency at p99 increased slightly, so we need to balance.
[00:50] Ethan: just to add context, our traffic has a really spiky diurnal pattern, plus batch sizes vary a lot — sometimes single requests, sometimes 12 at a time. the continuous batching you mentioned, how aggressive can that be without harming latency SLOs?
[01:10] Nina: good question. redwood's runtime will do adaptive batching but we can tune the window; for this poc we suggested conservative windows to hit your 200ms median target, but if you want to optimize cost more we can widen batching which helps throughput but might push p95/p99.
[01:33] Priya: from security, we also need clarity on KMS and HSM for model keys and audit log retention. we operate under a 7-year audit trail for some records and we need to ensure logs are immutable. is that covered in private deployment?
[01:54] Samir: yes, in Private you get customer-managed KMS integration and we can plug in HSM for key wrapping. audit logs and long-term retention are configurable; i'll share the SOC2 and deployment note post-call.
[02:12] Aaron: on the model front, the q4_2 quant seems promising for cost, but we did see mild regressions on clinical summarization prompts — some hallucination-like insertions. how did you measure quality delta?
[02:30] Nina: we used a mix of BLEU-ish metrics and a small human eval set of 100 prompts. regression was about 3-4% lower on strict information recall. the important piece is your canonical prompts, cause if your distribution is more extractive the quant might perform worse.
[02:46] Maya: exactly, most of our flows are extractive plus normalization, so we can't accept anything that deletes entities. this is a hard requirement.
[02:59] Samir: ok that's helpful, requirement: entity fidelity must be preserved. so our recommended approach is pin primary model to the high-fidelity variant for production route, and use a quantized fallback for bulk async jobs or for cost-sensitive endpoints.
[03:15] Ethan: could you define pinning? is that a hard pin so traffic never goes to new versions, or is it a canary that moves over time?
[03:29] Nina: there are options: hard pin (force a model version id), soft pin with shadow routing (traffic routed but responses not returned), and policy-based routing where you allow model variant swap only if metrics within threshold. for you, i'd recommend soft pin for the first 2 weeks and then lock after regression checks pass.
[03:48] Priya: related: what happens during a rollback? do you lose cached KV state, or is there a warm-start?
[04:03] Nina: good call. kv cache is per model version; switching versions may need to repopulate caches which can add a small spike to latency for the first few requests. to mitigate we do warm caches via shadow traffic or pre-warming batch requests.
[04:20] Lucas: noted — we'll schedule a warm-up window in the rollback plan. also, we should plan a dry-run so infra knows what to expect.
[04:31] Maya: on metrics, last week's shadow run numbers: median latency 160ms, p95 520ms, p99 980ms for primary model (base float), quantized variant had median 180ms, p95 640ms, p99 1.2s but cost per token was ~18% lower.
[04:53] Samir: thanks, that matches nina's numbers. ok so signposts: median still under target but p99 is close to your threshold. do you have SLOs?
[05:05] Ethan: SLO is 95% under 500ms for user-facing inference. so p95 above is an issue.
[05:15] Nina: to meet p95, we can do a couple levers: reduce batch windows, route high-priority traffic to dedicated instances (redwood dedicated), or keep a smaller family model for low-latency critical paths. There are cost tradeoffs in each.
[05:33] Maya: small-family model — you mean like a compact model from the same family with fewer params? will quality be acceptable?
[05:41] Nina: depends. smaller family often reduces hallucination but also can lose nuanced reasoning. for extractive tasks it may be fine. we'll evaluate on your prompt set.
[05:52] Priya: security question — if we use Dedicated or Private, network egress rules: can we keep all traffic within our V P C and use customer-managed routing?
[06:05] Samir: yes for Private deployment we can place inference in your VPC and enforce strict egress; for Dedicated we offer regional isolation but not full VPC peering by default. we can make exceptions under enterprise terms.
[06:18] Aaron: latency-wise, does Private deployment give better p99 since network hops are fewer?
[06:26] Nina: often yes, colocating reduces network tail latency and gives you deterministic kernel and hardware choices; but it's also more ops overhead.
[06:34] Maya: back to fallback plan — let's sketch an emergency flow. if p99 spikes > 1.5s or quality regression detected by golden set, what do we want to happen automatically?
[06:48] Samir: our suggested emergency fallback: 1) automatic divert to pinned smaller family optimized for latency (policy threshold), 2) if quality drop detected by eval or user feedback we route to manual override and contact infra. We can tier it: soft automatic fallback first, then manual.
[07:06] Ethan: how fast is an automated switch? seconds? minutes?
[07:11] Nina: the routing change itself is seconds but caches and downstream effects might take minutes for steady state. so plan for a 2-5 minute stabilization window.
[07:22] Maya: and the rollback dry-run — we'd like to simulate with shadow traffic and then do a controlled canary where 5% of traffic hits the fallback for 30 minutes.
[07:33] Lucas: we'll put that in the runbook. lucas: action item to coordinate times.
[07:40] Samir: on observability, you'll get token-level cost, per-route latencies, and model version dashboards. can we instrument a regression alert on entity-fidelity by running an auto-check against your golden set every 5 minutes?
[07:54] Aaron: we can, but we may need the ability to set thresholds per prompt type. some prompts are more sensitive than others.
[08:03] Nina: we support per-prompt tags in the eval harness; we'll set the sensitive flows to stricter thresholds.
[08:12] Priya: i want to call out compliance — audit logs, SSO. for SOC2 we need RBAC for key rotation and an audit trail for who bumped a pin or initiated a rollback. does the console record that?
[08:26] Samir: yes console has activity logs for rollout actions, and we can integrate with your SAML SSO for admin access. rotation is supported via your KMS.
[08:34] Maya: perfect. one more: what about model caching across versions — will the kv cache cause cross-version leakage of PII? we need to ensure cache eviction handles privacy work.
[08:48] Nina: KV cache is scoped to model version and instance; we can also configure strict cache zeroing on model switch and TTLs to meet privacy needs.
[08:57] Ethan: how about a concrete schedule: we want to finish the QA pass and agree pin policy by next tuesday. is that feasible?
[09:05] Samir: yes. proposed timeline: customer provides prompt sets by friday 2026-07-24, we run automated evals and hand-off human review over the weekend, on monday/tuesday we'll present matrix and recommend a pinning policy.
[09:19] Maya: ok we'll upload by friday.
[09:23] Nina: re: metrics, i'll include a 3-way cost/latency/quality table comparing: primary float model (v1.2.0), quant q4_2 (v1.2.0-q4_2), and smaller family model (m-fam-2.1). that gives you the tradeoffs.
[09:40] Aaron: curious about warm-cold cache behavior — can we pre-warm the kv for the model we plan to ramp to?
[09:48] Nina: yes we can push pre-warm requests via shadow traffic or a synthetic generator, we recommend a staged warm-up to avoid thrusting traffic spikes downstream.
[09:58] Lucas: let's capture two contingency plans: A) automatic soft fallback to quant variant, B) manual rollback to last known good version with pre-warm. both validated in a dry-run.
[10:10] Priya: security will require step-by-step playbook for manual rollback with who signs off. we need this in writing for our compliance team.
[10:20] Samir: we'll provide a written runbook with sign-off steps. lucas will coordinate.
[10:26] Maya: on the human eval, do you recommend blind review or inline diffing? we prefer blind so reviewers aren't biased by model name.
[10:34] Nina: blind review is better. we can produce side-by-side blinded diffs and a scorer UI.
[10:41] Ethan: last question — do you support routing based on request headers (priority flag) so we can route high-priority clinical lookups to dedicated nodes?
[10:55] Samir: yes header based routing is supported; you can tag requests and set policy routes in the console.
[11:03] Maya: great. any objections to proceeding with the plan?
[11:07] Priya: none, security wants the written runbook and the KMS note.
[11:11] Samir: noted. i'll follow up with SOC2 and private deployment notes. nina will run the matrix. lucas will propose rollback windows. maya you'll provide prompts.
[11:22] Lucas: i'll schedule the dry-run on 2026-07-30 as proposed, pending your infra availability, ethan.
[11:28] Ethan: sounds good, i'll check infra calendar.
[11:33] Samir: ok quick recap and next steps: 1) maya upload prompts by 2026-07-24; 2) nina run and share latency/cost/quality matrix by 2026-07-27; 3) samir share security brief by 2026-07-29; 4) lucas + ethan schedule dry-run for 2026-07-30.
[11:55] Maya: thanks everyone, appreciate the thoroughness.
[12:00] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and action items. bye.
